incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2374 detected on runtime-prod-usw2-01 — elevated CUDA OOM rate (8% OOMs over 10m) despite reported headroom ~6GB. Creating thread for live mitigation. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-oom (TL;DR: check reserves, fragmentation, KV cache, spill config).

jordan_oncall: oncall here. seeing spike in 10m OOMs, customers starting to surface errors. Marta, can you paste the example OOM log and allocator state?

marta_eng: sending the common log we see:```
[2026-03-15T12:04:21Z] cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at runtime/infer.cc:412
allocator: total_gpu=40GB free=6.1GB reserved_blocks=10 reserved_size=12GB
spare_pool: reported_free=5.5GB usable_free=1.2GB
kv_cache: entries=24k cached_bytes=9.8GB
fragmentation_metric: large_free_segments=2 avg_segment_size=600MB
```
Note the headroom number comes from driver free memory but `usable_free` is much lower. Looks like reserved blocks + kv cache + fragmentation make the reported headroom inaccurate.

lee_sre: that matches a "headroom illusion" pattern — driver reports free but allocator can't use because of reserved/fragmented slabs. Two quick mitigations we can attempt with low blast radius: 1) turn off prefix/KV caching for this node pool 2) reduce reserve allocation for the runtime (soft-reserve -> allow eviction).

marta_eng: here are the commands I have ready (canary first):

1) toggle kv cache off (runtime admin API):
```bash
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://runtime-admin.prod/api/v1/flags \
  -d '{"kv_cache.enabled":false}'
```

2) lower reserve threshold on canary node (will allow reserve eviction):
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://runtime-admin.prod/api/v1/nodes/runtime-prod-usw2-01 \
  -d '{"allocator.soft_reserve_mb": 512}'
```

3) if we need to drain a node for a rolling restart (canary then roll):
```bash
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

vincent_runtime: I can run the canary toggle on gpu-node-17 now. Will only flip KV cache and monitor.

jordan_oncall: do it, but check customer impact first. cs-rep, can you confirm which customers hit errors and whether it's critical?

cs-rep: I see three external tenants showing 5xx errors correlating with the spike (tenant-io, mediaforge, quickchat). I've opened tickets and flagged them P2. No SLA breach yet but elevated error rates for those tenants.

vincent_runtime: flipping kv_cache off on gpu-node-17 now.

ops-bot: [action] applied flag kv_cache.enabled=false to node gpu-node-17 by vincent_runtime at 2026-03-15T12:07:02Z

marta_eng: canary logs: OOMs on that node dropped immediately to near zero, allocator shows usable_free moved from 1.2GB -> 4.8GB, fragmentation unchanged but reserve blocks freed for eviction. Metrics: OOM rate cluster-wide down from 8% -> 2.1% in 2 minutes.

lee_sre: good signal. Next step: roll this flag across the affected nodes gradually (1 node / 2m) and meanwhile create a temporary safer fallback by lowering the soft-reserve cluster-wide. I'll coordinate the rollout.

jordan_oncall: agree. Vincent, can you start a rolling flag rollout to the remaining 4 nodes in the pool? One at a time, wait 120s between. I'll hold the pager for rollback if OOMs spike.

vincent_runtime: starting rollout — nodes: gpu-node-17,18,20,21,22. Sequence started.

marta_eng: also enabling spill-to-disk for large KV pages could help longer term. That's a heavier change; let's keep that for post-incident unless we see OOMs rebound during rollout.

ops-bot: [progress] kv_cache.enabled=false applied to gpu-node-18 at 2026-03-15T12:09:43Z

lee_sre: watching telemetry — OOM rate now 0.6% after 3 nodes updated. No new container crashes.

cs-rep: customer tickets updated: tenants notified we are mitigating, ETA 10–15m for full mitigation. No further errors reported from tenant-io and quickchat after canary updates.

vincent_runtime: rollout finished across pool at 2026-03-15T12:14:50Z.

marta_eng: cluster aggregate: OOM rate 0.4%, headroom reported still ~5.8GB but usable_free now ~4.9GB. We should close the immediate incident but follow up with a postmortem.

lee_sre: short-term mitigation decided: keep KV caching off for 2 hours, monitor. Action items for oncall/postmortem:
- Add telemetry that shows reserved vs usable free (surface whether reserves are evictable).
- Add an allocator metric for fragmentation (largest contiguous free chunk).
- Revisit reserve sizing logic: too-large reserved blocks reduce usable headroom under fragmentation.
- Run a lab repro with high KV cache occupancy to validate fallback behavior.

jordan_oncall: handing to oncall for post-incident follow-up. cs-rep to continue customer comms. I'll write the incident summary and schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow.

cs-rep: customers emailed with status and expected follow-up.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT 2374 -> mitigated (severity reduced). Timeline: 12:04 detected -> 12:07 canary -> 12:15 rollout complete -> 12:18 mitigated. Please file postmortem using template: https://internal/postmortems/new

lee_sre: reassigning to marta_eng for PM items and backlog. I'll add a follow-up task to the runtime repo to gate KV cache against fragmentation signals.

marta_eng: noted; will own the PM and add telemetry tickets. Thanks all for quick reaction. :thumbsup: 

jordan_oncall: closing live thread, leaving follow-ups in incidents board. If anything regresses ping me directly.
